RBI/DOR/2026-27/474
DOR.CAP.REC.300/21.06.201/2026-27

October 07, 2026

Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Credit Valuation Adjustment Framework) Directions, 2026

In exercise of the powers conferred by Sections 21 and 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank of India, being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in the public interest so to do, hereby issues the Directions hereinafter specified.

1. These Directions shall come into force from April 1, 2027 and shall apply to all commercial banks excluding regional rural banks, local area banks, small finance banks and payments banks.

2. A bank shall hold capital against the risk of mark-to-market losses on derivative positions arising from deterioration in counterparty credit quality, known as credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk.

3. A bank with an aggregate notional amount of non-centrally cleared derivatives of less than Rs 1,00,000 crore may choose to set its CVA capital equal to 100 per cent of its capital requirement for counterparty credit risk.

(Sunil T S Nair)
Chief General Manager
